cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: For Stability’s Sake
cards.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. Keep the treasurer's page out of the fair briefing. Our chair needs everyone's confidence today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She spent the stall money on that arch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. Call it donated decoration. If the stallholders find out, they'll replace her before we open.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cover the shortfall, but she must sign an IOU.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Privately, after her welcome. Let them see her opening the fair, not borrowing to open it.

mechanism: A copies a misunderstood sign of stable leadership, learns destabilizing truth, and protects the existing power balance by concealing it.
confusable: D61 protects A culpability; D63 protects existing balance because A believes disruption would be worse.
comparison: Competing department heads after resignation versus fair chair endangered by misused funds.
seedUse: Use resignation printout/speech and private IOU as distinct threats to public continuity.
